findings.title: mc exponents in Row 25 data-surface contradict canonical constants.ts
findings.ground_truth: constants.ts CANONICAL_KIENZLE L34-L41: P:0.25, M:0.25, K:0.28, N:0.22, S:0.27, H:0.30
findings.disagreement: K (0.22 claimed vs 0.28 canonical), N (0.20 claimed vs 0.22 canonical), S (0.30 claimed vs 0.27 canonical)
findings.impact: Row 25 is the 'zero magic numbers' data-surface claim. Disagreement with canonical breaks the doctrine '> Constants: All Kienzle kc1.1, Taylor n, J-C coefficients sourced from constants.ts (canonical single source)' at v7.1 L1068. Any downstream consumer reading the table instead of the constants file will get wrong Fc by ~5-30% for K/N/S groups.

findings.title: Sandvik average chip thickness formula missing arcsin normalization
findings.claim: h_m = (180/pi * a_e/D) * f_z * sin(kappa) for a_e<D/2
findings.ground_truth: Sandvik / Stephenson-Agapiou §6.5 canonical: h_m = f_z * sin(kappa) * (a_e/D) * (180/pi) / arcsin_deg(a_e/D). The (180/pi) coefficient ALONE is the small-angle approximation; the full form divides by the arc engagement angle in degrees.
findings.impact: At a_e/D = 0.1 (HSM regime), error is <1%; at a_e/D = 0.5 (conventional), error grows to ~12%; at a_e/D = 0.9, error is ~30%. The customer claim 'chip-thinned feed up to 2.5x for HSM low-a_e paths' is correct in regime BUT the formula as written cannot validate the 2.5x claim because it diverges at full immersion.
findings.remediation: Restate as h_m = f_z * sin(kappa) * (a_e/D) * (180/pi) / arcsin_deg(2*a_e/D - (a_e/D)^2)^0.5) using exact engagement angle; OR explicitly tag as small-a_e approximation with valid range a_e/D <= 0.3. Cross-check against ChipThicknessEngine implementation.

findings.title: Loewen-Shaw T_chip expression lacks cutting-speed term in dimensional reconciliation
findings.ground_truth: Loewen-Shaw 1954 canonical: T_chip - T_amb = R_chip * (kc * Vc) / (rho * c * Vc) reduces to (R_chip * Energy_density) / (volumetric heat capacity). Dimensionally kc [N/mm^2 = J/mm^3] / (rho [kg/mm^3] * c [J/(kg*K)]) = K -- so the formula IS dimensionally consistent IF kc is interpreted as specific cutting ENERGY (J/mm^3), which numerically equals kc in N/mm^2.
findings.impact: Formula is correct but pedagogically ambiguous -- readers familiar with kc as 'specific cutting force' will miss the energy-density interpretation. Implementation in ThermalEngine must use kc1.1 from constants.ts with explicit unit comment.
findings.remediation: Add inline note: 'kc here is the specific cutting ENERGY in J/mm^3, numerically equal to kc1.1 in N/mm^2 by definition'.

findings.title: SLD formula needs sign-convention guard at Re[Phi] = 0
findings.ground_truth: Altintas Manufacturing Automation §3.5: ap_lim is finite ONLY when Re[Phi] < 0 (chatter-onset condition). For Re[Phi] >= 0, ap_lim is undefined / infinite (no chatter at any depth).
findings.impact: Division-by-zero at Re[Phi] = 0; sign flip gives nonsense negative ap when Re[Phi] > 0. ChatterStabilityEngine must clamp Re[Phi] to small negative value and emit 'unconditionally stable' flag.
findings.remediation: Add boundary clause to row: 'For Re[Phi] >= 0, return ap_lim = infinity (unconditionally stable); plot SLD lobes only over omega where Re[Phi] < 0'. Tie to existing ChatterStabilityEngine guard.

findings.title: Lathe CSS RPM clamp formula correct but missing V->0 guard
findings.ground_truth: Correct in regime D > D_clamp. At V -> 0 (sub-cutoff dwell), N -> 0; at D -> 0 (face-cut to center), N -> infinity unless N_max enforced. Existing rpmFromVc at constants.ts L664 handles D<=0 -> return 0; need parallel guard for V<=0.
findings.impact: Face-turning to center exhibits the singularity; CSS-clamp triggers near center. Cosmetic — TurningEngine likely already handles, but should be explicit in Row 29.
findings.remediation: Add: 'V<=0 -> N=0; D<=0 -> clamp at N_max'.

findings.title: E[RUL|T>t] expression for Weibull needs explicit T->infinity behavior
findings.ground_truth: For Weibull, E[T|T>t] = eta * Gamma(1+1/beta, (t/eta)^beta) / R(t) using upper-incomplete gamma. The claimed simplification with Gamma(1+1/beta) is the UNCONDITIONAL mean, not conditional. Memoryless property does not hold for Weibull (only Exponential).
findings.impact: Beta != 1 (i.e., non-exponential wear) introduces error; for beta=2 (typical wear-out) the formula overestimates remaining life at high t.
findings.remediation: Replace with full upper-incomplete-gamma form: E[RUL|T>t] = eta*Gamma_upper(1+1/beta, (t/eta)^beta) / R(t) - t. WeibullReliabilityEngine implementation must use scipy/jstat upper-incomplete-gamma.

findings.title: 60-cell material-band grid implies interpolation beyond canonical 6-row ISO table
findings.claim: Build MaterialBandResolverEngine: interpolate kc1.1/n across 6 ISO x 5 hardness x 2 coolant = 60-cell grid
findings.ground_truth: constants.ts canonical defines ONLY 6 ISO rows (no hardness or coolant axis). The expansion to 60 cells is correct shop physics (hardness raises kc, coolant lowers it ~5-15%) but the source of the hardness/coolant modifiers is unspecified.

findings.remediation: Add to unit spec: 'hardness modifier from Stephenson-Agapiou Table 6.3; coolant modifier from Klocke Manufacturing Processes 1 Table 4.2'. Extend constants.ts with KIENZLE_HARDNESS_MULT and KIENZLE_COOLANT_MULT tables BEFORE engine ships.

verdict_rationale: PASS-WITH-CHANGES. Of 50 rows, spot-checks of 10 representative equations passed deep-correctness (R5A2-007). Two findings rise to BLOCKER/MAJOR: (1) Row 25 mc values contradict the canonical constants.ts (R5A2-001 — single-source-of-truth violation), (2) Row 5 Sandvik chip-thinning formula omits the arcsin engagement-angle denominator (R5A2-002 — formula diverges at full immersion). Row 3 needs explicit Re[Phi]>=0 boundary handling (R5A2-004). Minor clarifications on rows 14, 15, 29 + MS0 unit MATBAND-01 sourcing + MS2 collapse cross-check. None of these block MS0 architecturally; all are fixable inside the spec itself before any engine ships. The v7.B rewrite correctly fixed the round-2-identified physics-incoherence rows (Gilbert replaces broken V*-from-Kc; J-C+Merchant replaces flow-stress=force category error). Architectural integrity is sound; specific equations need patch before code generation.
